invariants: reader and writer protocols each expose one caller-buffer partial-transfer primitive
protocol operations return one portable Result<Int, Error> progress contract
MemoryReader implements Reader with the portable result contract
MemoryWriter implements Writer with the portable result contract
existing inherent MemoryReader and MemoryWriter methods remain source compatible
concrete protocol calls use imported qualified static dispatch
reader output storage is borrowed mutably and never retained
writer input storage is borrowed read-only and never retained
partial transfer reports an exact count without a payload allocation
exact memory reads validate limits and complete availability before mutation
allocating read and readExact remain bounded convenience methods
writer range bounds are validated before output mutation
TransferPolicy owns maximum transfer and reusable buffer byte ceilings
copy never reads a probe byte beyond its maximum transfer ceiling
copy retries partial writes from the exact unwritten range
successful zero write progress is a typed WriteZero error
CopyOutcome distinguishes observed source end from policy limit
consumer-defined imported Reader and Writer implementations are monomorphized without dynamic dispatch
ReplayBuffer validates requested length against its ceiling before source access
ReplayBuffer stages source progress in adapter-owned storage and publishes caller output only on exact success
failed exact reads retain their partial prefix for the next logical read
replay success advances a logical cursor without claiming that the underlying source cursor rolled back
replay scratch length bounds each source read to the exact remaining request
replay storage is compacted without allocating another payload buffer
unbounded readAll copy and implicit buffering are absent
unsupported: file socket and reactor protocol implementations
